Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Weather Newsletters BBC visits wildfire front in haze-choked Indonesia As Indonesia battles its worst wildfire season in a decade, a toxic haze is choking millions of residents in the region.
The BBC's Liza Tambunan is in central Kalimantan, where air pollution levels have plunged to hazardous levels.
The haze has been linked to hundreds of thousands of respiratory illnesses in Indonesia, and has drifted to neighbouring countries like Singapore and Malaysia.
Share Save Watch: Hong Kong crowds queue to see Van Gogh painting unveiled for first time in 60 years Châtaigniers en fleurs, also known as Chestnut Trees in Blossom, is expected to receive record bids at auction this weekend.
Buildings swept away as flash floods hit central Nepal A flash flood at the Budhi Gandaki River has swept away several buildings and bridges, two months after catastrophic floods hit the country.
Heavy police presence and barricading at Delhi's Jantar Mantar Tens of thousands of security personnel have been deployed and roads barricaded in Delhi to stop the latest Cockroach Janta Party demonstration.
Thai Queen makes first solo flight in fighter jet Thailand’s Queen Suthida made her first solo flight in a fighter jet, according to the Thai Royal Household.
Watch: Moment a government building collapses into a river in Nepal amid floods The municipality building in Baglung was left teetering on an unstable ledge due to floods before it fell into a river.
Bangkok declares disaster as heavy rains spark flooding Days of near continuous downpours have caused widespread flooding in the Thai capital.
Rare look at the remote engine rooms fuelling China's AI boom The BBC is in Inner Mongolia where dozen of Chinese data centres are being constructed, as the country aims to lead the world in artificial intelligence.
Watch: Six-year-old girl from China sets new Rubik's Cube world record Lian Yunzhi broke the women's world record twice in three days at World Cube Association competitions.
Watch: Dramatic moment a cargo ship crashes into another vessel Verified footage appears to show a cargo ship colliding with a fishing boat near Singapore, with investigators still working to establish exactly when and how the crash happened.
Inside Singapore's 'Fort Knox' for city's $2bn dirty money case auction The BBC goes inside a fortified storage facility to view luxury goods seized by police that are now up for auction.
What we know about the fatal Philippines ferry fire Rescuers are searching for survivors after the vessel travelling from the mainland to a popular tourist destination caught fire.
'A rare moment of joy': Nepal tunnel rescues bring hope for more flood survivors There are still hundreds of workers trapped in a network of tunnels that run along the Trishuli river.
Watch: Moment workers are rescued from Nepal tunnel Rescuers pull two people from a hydropower tunnel more than a week after a massive flash flood devastated the Nepal-China border.
Nepal says it will need billions in funding to rebuild after flash floods BBC South Asia correspondent Azadeh Moshiri is in Nepal where authorities are trying to begin rebuilding amid the debris.
Could robots be the future of theme parks? Galaxy Robot Park is a 16,500-square-meter venue in South Korea, with attractions including humanoid robots dancing to K-pop hits.
Nepal tunnel rescuers hunt for survivors with rafts and drone South Asian correspondent Azadeh Moshiri is at the site of a tunnel where rescuers still hope to find survivors following the Nepal-Tibet floods.
'Nothing but mud and silt' - the village swept away by deadly floods in Nepal BBC South Asia correspondent Azadeh Moshiri spoke to a local, who is still waiting for his his wife's body to be retrieved, as rescue efforts continue.
'It's hard to balance emotions and professionalism' says Nepal rescuer Helicopter pilot, Bibek Khadka, has told the BBC that families with missing loved ones have been reaching out to him for help.
Why US troops have a history in this raucous Thai city The BBC's Jonathan Head looks at the historical echoes of US troops arriving in Pattaya, a beach resort famous for its racy bars.
Cup noodles made with cold water? BBC tries Japan's viral snack The BBC's Tokyo correspondent Kurumi Mori tries Japan's latest food trend, instant noodles made using cold water.
